questions.text: An autoregressive model provides normalized conditional probabilities p(x_i | x_<i). How does it obtain the joint probability of a complete sequence?

options.A: Average the conditional probabilities across sequence positions.
options.B: Multiply the conditional probabilities across sequence positions.
options.C: Use only the conditional probability of the final sequence element.
options.D: Subtract the probability of generated sequences from one.

questions.explanation: The probability chain rule gives p(x) = product_i p(x_i | x_<i). Equivalently, log p(x) is the sum of the conditional log-probabilities.

questions.text: A proposed generator can draw realistic samples in one forward pass but exposes no tractable probability-density evaluator. You need exact log-likelihoods for arbitrary inputs. What should you conclude?

options.A: Fast sampling alone is sufficient to recover exact input likelihoods.
options.B: A discriminator score is automatically a normalized input density.
options.C: Drawing more samples makes each input's exact likelihood directly available.
options.D: The sampling interface does not meet the requirement; use a tractable explicit-density model.

questions.explanation: A sampler without a tractable density evaluator does not provide exact log-likelihoods. A model with tractable explicit density, such as a suitable autoregressive model or normalizing flow, addresses that requirement. Discriminator scores are not normalized data densities.

questions.text: This histogram estimator divides the fraction of samples in a bin by its width. What does it print?
questions.explanation: The bin is approximately [-0.1, 0.3), containing 0.0, 0.1, and 0.2. The density is 3 / (4 * 0.4) = 1.875. A density may exceed 1; the probability mass for this bin is density times width = 0.75.
